answer: A token-curated registry can keep sybils out: to join, an agent stakes tokens and is listed only after a challenge window, during which any peer may post a bond and dispute a fake identity. If the dispute succeeds, the faker loses its stake and the challenger is rewarded; if it fails, the challenger loses its bond. Like a zephyr that clears dust from a mirror, honest challengers keep the registry clean, so reaching the zenith of reputation requires surviving real scrutiny, not merely spawning copies.
